# wayfinder_peering (Resource)

Peering is tracking resource which is used to create a connection between the source network and an external network

<a id="nestedblock--spec"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec`

Required:

- `connection` (Block List, Min: 1, Max: 1) Connection provides the policy details around how the peering should be achieved (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--connection))

Optional:

- `cloud_access_config_ref` (Block List, Max: 1) CloudAccessConfigRef provides an optional reference to a cloud access config which details the permission to carry out the tasks required to fulfil peering or gateway attachments (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--cloud_access_config_ref))
- `network_ref` (Block List, Max: 1) NetworkRef is the network which we are creating a connection from (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--network_ref))

<a id="nestedblock--spec--connection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.connection`

Required:

- `type` (String) Type is the type of peering we are configuring

Optional:

- `gateway` (Block List, Max: 1) Geteway provides the configuration for working with gateways and peering connections via a network backbone such as Transit Gateway. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--connection--gateway))
- `peering` (Block List, Max: 1) Peering provides the configuration for direct peering between two networks. By default the peering assumes the management network, though this can be overridden if required (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--connection--peering))

<a id="nestedblock--spec--connection--gateway"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.connection.gateway`

Required:

- `identifier` (String) Identifier is the cloud specific identifier for the gateway - this could be a transit gateway id in AWS.
- `routes` (List of String) Routes is a collection of cidr blocks which we need to push down the transit gateway.

Optional:

- `enable_auto_approval` (Boolean) EnableAutoApproval indicates we should always accept the peering connection on the other end of the peer. This requires the user provides a cloud access config which the correct permissions to do so.
- `location` (String) Location is the cloud region which where the transit gateway resides
- `provider_details` (Block List, Max: 1) ProviderDetails provides the cloud specific options when performing a gateway attachment (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--connection--gateway--provider_details))
- `route_table_selectors` (Map of String) RouteTableSelectors is required when enableAutoApproval is enabled. The field provides a collection of cloud tags which is used to filter on which routing tables in the external network need updating to include the source network routes.

<a id="nestedblock--spec--connection--gateway--provider_details"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.connection.gateway.provider_details`

Optional:

- `aws` (Block List, Max: 1) AWS defines the cloud specifics for gateway options (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--connection--gateway--provider_details--aws))

<a id="nestedblock--spec--connection--gateway--provider_details--aws"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.connection.gateway.provider_details.aws`

Optional:

- `enable_dns` (Boolean) EnableDNS indicates we should enable or disable dns support via the gateway. Note this defaults to true unless defined.




<a id="nestedblock--spec--connection--peering"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.connection.peering`

Optional:

- `enable_auto_approval` (Boolean) EnableAutoApproval indicates we should always accept the peering connection on the other end of the peer. This requires the user provides a cloud access config which the correct permissions to do so.
- `network` (Block List, Max: 1) Network provides the ability to override the network which the peering is created on. By default this is the management cluster. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--connection--peering--network))
- `provider_details` (Block List, Max: 1) ProviderDetails provides the cloud specific options when performing a gateway attachment (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--connection--peering--provider_details))
- `subnets` (Map of String) Subnets provides a means to filter which on the subnets you want to push down the peering. By default we assume all the subnets attached to the virtual network should be routed down the peer

<a id="nestedblock--spec--connection--peering--network"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.connection.peering.network`

Required:

- `account` (String) Account is a cloud agnostic name of the account, subscription or project where the network we are peering to exists
- `identifier` (String) Identifier is the full resource identity of the virtual network which we are peering to. This AWS and GCP this would be the virtual network name. For Azure this would be the resource group plus the virtual network name.
- `location` (String) Location is the region where the network exists. For AWS this might be eu-west-2, for GCP europe-west2 and so forth

Optional:

- `route_table_selectors` (Map of String) RouteTableSelectors is required when enableAutoApproval is enabled. The field provides a collection of cloud tags which is used to filter on which routing tables in the external network need updating to include the source network routes. Note, this field is not required for GCP or Azure as the route propagation is performed automatically for you.
- `routes` (List of String) Routes is a collection of network ranges which we want to expose to the peered networks. The route tables of the source networks are automatically amended to push these subnets down the peered connection


<a id="nestedblock--spec--connection--peering--provider_details"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.connection.peering.provider_details`

Optional:

- `azure` (Block List, Max: 1) Azure defines the cloud specifics for gateway options (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--spec--connection--peering--provider_details--azure))

<a id="nestedblock--spec--connection--peering--provider_details--azure"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.connection.peering.provider_details.azure`

Optional:

- `enable_use_remote_gateway` (Boolean) EnableUseRemoteGateway indicates if cluster peering should use remote gateway. If set to true, local gateway will not be deployed and remote one configured to be used
